This file builds monomorphized Stable MIR bodies and then hands them to the converter; if async-closure MIR reaches SMIR at all, this is the immediate upstream entry point feeding the failing conversion path.

Defines the StableMIR body schema that the converter must populate. If async-closure/coroutine MIR has no matching stable representation, the failure would surface here as an unsupported lowering gap.

Async closures are lowered into MIR rvalues and aggregates here. The failing SMIR path likely sees the MIR shape produced by this lowering, so it is a strong upstream source of the unsupported construct.

This file classifies and type-checks closure and coroutine expressions, including async closures. If the closure kind or signature is misclassified, that would propagate into the MIR shape that SMIR cannot lower.
Defines the closure/coroutine capture and closure-kind data used across lowering. Async-closure handling depends on these types, so this is a key semantic source for the unsupported path.
Destination-based expression lowering can emit closure- and coroutine-related control flow and temporaries. It is a plausible producer of the MIR form that later trips the SMIR converter.

This is where async closure syntax is lowered from AST into later IR. If the desugaring shape is not one SMIR supports, the issue can originate here even though it only becomes visible at SMIR conversion time.
Async closures share the coroutine/state-machine lowering pipeline. This pass can introduce or preserve MIR forms that Stable MIR still needs explicit support for.
SMIR type conversion for closure/coroutine-related types lives here. If async closures need additional type-side support alongside the MIR lowering gap, this is the closest companion file to inspect.
